conventions.convention: A four-square representation is an ordered integer quadruple; two representations are equivalent up to signs and order exactly when their multisets of absolute coordinate values agree.
Euler's four-square identity uses the displayed Conrad sign pattern; this exact pattern makes all four bilinear coordinates divisible by the descent modulus when the input quadruples are congruent.
The least absolute remainder modulo positive m is the unique r with −m < 2r ≤ m; for even m the tie is resolved as +m/2.
The relative Frobenius of a finite-field extension with base field of order q is x ↦ x^q.
A normal basis is a basis consisting of the full Galois orbit of one element; an ordering of the Galois group supplies the corresponding ordered basis.
A primitive n-th root of unity has exact multiplicative order n; an arbitrary n-th root need not be primitive, and μ_n(K) need not have n elements.
The cyclotomic extension K(μ_n) is the splitting field of t^n−1; describing it as K(ζ_n) requires a primitive n-th root, supplied when the characteristic does not divide n.

Cyclotomic polynomials are defined recursively in Z[t] by the divisor-product identity, with exact divisibility established by the following theorem; they are not defined as minimal polynomials or initially by their complex roots.
The formula Q(μ_m) ∩ Q(μ_n) = Q(μ_gcd(m,n)) is restricted to rational cyclotomic fields; the analogous statement over a general base field is not asserted.
Throughout the Noetherian development rings are commutative and unital, the zero ring is allowed unless explicitly excluded, and a Noetherian ring means its regular module is Noetherian.

The implication from the ascending-chain condition to the maximal-ideal condition uses dependent choice, while the maximal non-finitely-generated ideal used for Cohen's criterion uses Zorn's lemma and hence full choice.
The leading-coefficient ideal at stage n uses polynomials of exact degree n and adjoins 0 because the zero polynomial has no degree; the stages begin at n=0.

Noether's invariant-ring theorem uses the full orbit polynomial over a finite group, allowing repeated factors, and does not require the group order to be invertible; invertibility is required only for the Reynolds-operator example.

load_bearing.statement: For a commutative ring R, the following are equivalent: R is Noetherian; every ideal is finitely generated; every ascending sequence of ideals stabilises; every nonempty set of ideals has a maximal member. Only ACC ⇒ maximal condition uses dependent choice.
For n≥1, Φ₁=t−1 and Φ_n=(t^n−1)/∏_{d|n, 0<d<n}Φ_d in Z[t], with the asserted exact division and divisor-product identity justified by the following theorem.
If E/F_q has degree n, then E/F_q is Galois and Gal(E/F_q) is cyclic of order n, generated by x ↦ x^q.
For the four displayed bilinear coordinates z₁,z₂,z₃,z₄ with the stated sign pattern, (x₁²+x₂²+x₃²+x₄²)(y₁²+y₂²+y₃²+y₄²)=z₁²+z₂²+z₃²+z₄².
If p is prime, 1<m<p, and pm is a sum of four integer squares, then pn is a sum of four integer squares for some integer n with 1≤n<m.
Every prime p has integers a,b,c,d with p=a²+b²+c²+d².
Every nonnegative integer n has integers a,b,c,d with n=a²+b²+c²+d².
For a field K and n≥1, μ_n(K)={x∈K:x^n=1}; a primitive n-th root of unity is an element of exact multiplicative order n.
Every finite Galois extension K/F has an element α whose full family of Galois conjugates is an ordered F-basis of K.
For every n≥1, Φ_n is irreducible in Q[t].
If gcd(n,q)=1 and d is the order of [q] in (Z/n)×, then Φ_n over F_q is a product of φ(n)/d pairwise distinct monic irreducibles, each of degree d.
If R is a Noetherian commutative ring, then R[x] is Noetherian; zero divisors and the zero ring are allowed.
Over a Noetherian commutative ring, an R-module is Noetherian if and only if it is finitely generated, if and only if it is finitely presented.
A commutative algebra module-finite over a Noetherian commutative ring is Noetherian; when the base embeds, every intermediate ring is module-finite over the base and Noetherian.
If A⊆B⊆C, A is Noetherian, C is of finite type over A, and C is module-finite over B, then B is of finite type over A.
If A is Noetherian, C is a finite-type A-algebra containing A, and a finite group G acts on C by A-algebra automorphisms, then C^G is of finite type over A.
A commutative ring in which every prime ideal is finitely generated is Noetherian; the proof uses Zorn's lemma.

concerns.concern: The Statement says the attainable residues are exactly 0 through 6. The proof exhausts the possible residue classes but does not explicitly supply witnesses showing every listed class is attained; the witness choices are immediate from the same parity cases.

Refutation step 1.1 states the truncated formula for Φ_105 from the divisor recursion, but the explanation about dropping factors of degree at least 15 suppresses the algebra that converts the recursion to the displayed rational product. The omitted finite calculation is checkable and the resulting coefficient −2 is correct.
